chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

There is no Jumuʿah upon the people of the villages, nor going out for the two ʿEids. The aspect of it here also is taqiyyah, and it is possible that what is meant is one whose village is farther from the town by more than two farsakhs, and in whom there is not the number by which Jumuʿah becomes obligatory upon them, nor have their conditions been fulfilled among them.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقُرَىٰ: the people of villages or rural settlements
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary concealment in a context of risk
key_terms.الْعَدَدُ: the required number of people for the legal validity or obligation
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two ʿEid prayers, ʿEid al-Fiṭr and ʿEid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْنِ: two farsakhs, a measure of distance

ai.seo_question: Are the people of villages obligated to establish Jumuʿah and attend the ʿEid prayer?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling regarding Jumuʿah and the ʿEid prayer for villagers. It indicates that the ruling may be understood through taqiyyah, or as applying to those villages distant from the town and lacking the required number and conditions for Jumuʿah.
